literal: He who says he desires freedom from contempt, let him guard his own mind against stealing even a single thing of whatever small measure.
translation: He who wishes not to be despised by others must guard his own mind against the thought of stealing anything, however small.
modern: பிறரால் இகழப்படாமல் வாழ விரும்புகிறேன் என்று சொல்பவன், எந்த ஒரு சிறிய பொருளையும் திருட நினைக்காதவாறு தன் நெஞ்சைக் காத்துக் கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet explains that self-respect and avoiding the scorn of others begin with mental discipline. If a person desires to live without being looked down upon, they must protect their mind from even the slightest thought of theft. The word 'eḷḷāmai' refers to the state of not being despised, and 'kaḷḷāmai' refers to non-stealing. The poet emphasizes that even a tiny, hidden desire to take what belongs to another can ruin one's honor, so the mind itself must be guarded.
